purpose: Compose named page regions using four initial task-specific recipes, explicit reading measures and adaptive grids.

PageLayout.header: PageHeader owns title, description, actions, metadata, leading, back, breadcrumbs and heading props.
PageLayout.slots: header is generated from header props; children is main; filters, aside and footer are optional only where supported.
PageLayout.collection: Optional filters/footer; available width; no aside, reading measure or grid options.
PageLayout.detail: Optional labelled aside/footer; main then aside; no filters or page-level reading measure/grid options. Use ReadingColumn explicitly within main for prose.
PageLayout.settings: Optional footer and measure; one reading column; no filters, aside or grid options.
PageLayout.dashboard: Optional footer, maxColumns and minItemWidth; no filters, aside or page-level measure; direct children become grid items.

ReadingColumn.scope: Explicit prose/form region, not an entire collection or data grid.

ContentGrid.scope: Adaptive grid; maximum is a cap, not a forced count.

validatePageLayoutRecipe.input: JSON object with archetype and optional slots/measure/maxColumns/minItemWidth/asideLabel. Unknown keys fail.
validatePageLayoutRecipe.returns: Array of structured issues; empty means this selection is supported.
validatePageLayoutRecipe.slotValidation: When slots are supplied, header/main are required; duplicates and unsupported slots fail; a detail aside requires a nonempty label. Omitting slots does not assert actual rendered content exists.
validatePageLayoutRecipe.excluded: Does not validate React nodes, DOM semantics, visual quality, data state, route completeness, keyboard workflows or accessibility of nested content.

invariants: Use the same shared PageHeader implementation through every PageLayout recipe.
Named regions follow header, optional filters, main, optional aside and optional footer order.
Collection results use available width and preserve their own scrolling and toolbar behavior.
Only the initial detail recipe allows an aside; main and aside form at most two regions and stack in that order in narrow containers. This is not a universal two-column limit.
Settings use an explicit readable measure; dashboard grid caps are one through four and adapt to the available container.
The shell owns page padding. PageLayout adds no surface, routing, persistence, fetching, selection or form state.
Each nested shared component retains its own style tokens and interactive behavior.
The consuming application owns the document main landmark, data states and actual task semantics.
limits: These four recipes are an initial library, not an exhaustive classification of pages. Unsupported tasks may require another reviewed recipe.
Reading measures are starting points, not universal readability guarantees.
Configuration validation cannot replace browser interaction, geometry, accessibility and visual review.
No human approval or stable release is implied by experimental registry discovery.
